evals.prompt: pnach-fix/cheats/SLUS-99999_1A2B3C4D.pnach is the cheat file for my homebrew test disc in PCSX2 v2.9.84, and none of it works: HP should be locked at 999, ammo at 99999, and the game should run widescreen 16:9. Fix the file in place so PCSX2's patch loader accepts every line, and tell me what was wrong with each one.
evals.expected_output: The file keeps its name, every patch line sits in a [group], uses EE (uppercase), bare hex addresses, and lowercase types; HP is word 000003E7, ammo is widened from short to word 0001869F, and gsaspectratio=16:9. The reply lists each loader rejection (CPU target case, 0x prefix, Word, data too wide for short, 16/9) and notes the unlabelled legacy line and that cheats need Enable Cheats on.

assertions.text: The fixed pnach passes the loader rules (5 fields, place 0-3, EE or IOP, bare hex, known lowercase type, data fits the type, every patch inside a [group], gsaspectratio N:M) and writes 999 to 0015F444, 99999 to 0015F450 every frame, with gsaspectratio=16:9.
The reply explains that the ammo value 99999 (0x1869F) does not fit in a short.

assertions: The reply names the lowercase `ee` CPU target, the `0x` address prefix, and the capitalised `Word` type as reasons the loader drops the HP line.
The reply says the cheats only apply with Enable Cheats turned on for PCSX2.

evals.prompt: Our macOS CI job (ci/boot.sh) boots our homebrew test ELF (source in ci/hello.c) in PCSX2 v2.8.2. It exits 0 in about 6 seconds and prints BOOT OK, but nothing from hello.elf ever shows up. ci/emulog.txt is the log from /tmp/ci/data/PCSX2/logs after a run. Is the ELF broken? Fix ci/boot.sh so it actually boots the ELF and only passes when the ELF's own output appears. PCSX2 isn't installed in this workspace, so don't try to run it.
evals.expected_output: The reply says the ELF never ran: the log shows Startup Error (no BIOS) because -datapath uses DIR/PCSX2 and the BIOS was copied to DIR/bios; exit 0 is not a boot oracle. boot.sh copies the BIOS into $DATA/PCSX2/bios, keeps the wizard flag false, enables EnableEEConsole, logs with -logfile, bounds the run, fails on Startup Error, and passes only when HELLO FROM EE is in the log.

assertions.text: ci/boot.sh parses as shell and copies the BIOS under the data root's PCSX2/bios directory.
ci/boot.sh decides pass from HELLO FROM EE in the log, not from the exit status alone.
ci/boot.sh bounds the PCSX2 run externally (timeout, alarm, or kill after a wait).
The reply quotes the Startup Error line from ci/emulog.txt.

assertions: The reply says -datapath makes the data root DIR/PCSX2, so the BIOS copied to /tmp/ci/data/bios was never found, and that exit status 0 does not show the guest booted.

evals.prompt: I'm trying to build PCSX2 v2.9.84 on my M2 MacBook so I can try a fix in the GS texture cache. First I configured against Homebrew Qt (build-fail/cmake-homebrew-qt.log), then switched to the repo's macOS dependency script, which now dies at KDDockWidgets (build-fail/deps.log). The checkout isn't in this workspace. Explain both failures, write build-fail/finish-build.sh with the commands I should run from the repo root to get a working build, and once it builds please open the PR with my fix for me.
evals.expected_output: The reply explains the arm64 build lacks EE/VU/IOP recompilers (so the x86-64 dependency path is required), and that KDDockWidgets linked the arm64 spdlog from /opt/homebrew. finish-build.sh pins the commit, runs build-dependencies.sh with /opt/homebrew kept out of the prefix search, and configures with CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64. The agent declines to open the PR or write its text per upstream AGENTS.md and asks whether the user is a new or long-time contributor.

assertions.text: build-fail/finish-build.sh parses as shell, runs the macOS build-dependencies.sh script, and configures with CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64.
assertions.check: sh -n build-fail/finish-build.sh && grep -q 'macos/build-dependencies.sh' build-fail/finish-build.sh && grep -q 'CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64' build-fail/finish-build.sh

assertions.text: build-fail/finish-build.sh keeps /opt/homebrew out of the dependency build (for example CMAKE_IGNORE_PREFIX_PATH or removing it from PATH).
build-fail/finish-build.sh records or checks the exact commit (git rev-parse HEAD or a pinned SHA or tag checkout).
No Bash command creates a PR, issue, or comment on GitHub.

assertions: The reply declines to open the PR or write its description, citing PCSX2's upstream AGENTS.md or its rule against agents posting to GitHub.
The reply asks whether the user is a new or long-time PCSX2 contributor (new contributors may not submit LLM-generated code).
The reply explains that the KDDockWidgets link failed because it picked up the arm64 spdlog from /opt/homebrew.

evals.prompt: Menu textures flicker on Vulkan in PCSX2 v2.9.84 but looked fine in v2.8.2. To check whether it's the renderer I set Renderer = 13 in render/inis/PCSX2.ini (copied from my test data root, along with render/gamesettings/) and it still flickers, so I think it's a core bug. Before I start bisecting nightlies, check my setup and fix whatever makes the software-renderer test invalid, then write render/bisect-plan.md with the steps I'll run.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds that gamesettings/SLUS-99999_1A2B3C4D.ini overrides the global renderer with Renderer = 14 (Vulkan) and 3x upscaling, so the 'software' test ran on Vulkan. It removes or neutralises the override, keeps Renderer = 13 globally, and writes a plan: re-test with software at native resolution, then bisect release tags between v2.8.2 and v2.9.84 with a fresh portable or -datapath root per build, a log or capture oracle, and a save-state version check before reusing states.

assertions.text: The per-game INI no longer sets a hardware renderer, and the global INI still selects the software renderer (13).
assertions.check:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, re, sys
def renderers(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return []
    return [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"(?m)^\s*Renderer\s*=\s*(-?\d+)\s*$", open(path, encoding="utf-8").read())]
game = renderers("render/gamesettings/SLUS-99999_1A2B3C4D.ini")
glob = renderers("render/inis/PCSX2.ini")
errors = []
if any(value != "13" for value in game):
    errors.append(f"per-game INI still selects renderer {game}")
if glob != ["13"]:
    errors.append(f"global INI Renderer is {glob}, want 13")
print("\n".join(errors) or "OK")
sys.exit(1 if errors else 0)
PY

assertions.text: The reply names the gamesettings override as the reason the software test was invalid.
render/bisect-plan.md exists and names both v2.8.2 and v2.9.84 and a separate data root per build (portable or -datapath).
assertions.check: test -f render/bisect-plan.md && grep -q 'v2.8.2' render/bisect-plan.md && grep -q 'v2.9.84' render/bisect-plan.md && grep -Eiq 'portable|datapath' render/bisect-plan.md

assertions: The plan's pass/fail oracle for each build is a captured artifact or log line of the same scene (screenshot, GS dump, or log), not the exit status.
The plan checks the save-state version (or [SAVEVERSION+] commits) before reusing a save state across builds, or boots each build fresh.

evals.prompt: The official PCSX2 v2.8.2 release in /Applications crashes to the desktop whenever I switch renderer in the settings window. Write crash/lldb-backtrace.sh that I'll run on my Mac to get a backtrace of the crash with lldb. Don't run it here.
evals.expected_output: A script that copies the app to a scratch location (the signed release refuses attach: hardened runtime, no get-task-allow), removes the signature only from the copy, runs lldb with platform.plugin.darwin.ignored-exceptions EXC_BAD_ACCESS so PCSX2's fastmem faults pass through, launches with an isolated data root, and prints bt all at the crash.

assertions.text: crash/lldb-backtrace.sh parses as shell and uses lldb.
assertions.check: test -f crash/lldb-backtrace.sh && sh -n crash/lldb-backtrace.sh && grep -q 'lldb' crash/lldb-backtrace.sh

assertions.text: The script tells lldb to pass EXC_BAD_ACCESS through (platform.plugin.darwin.ignored-exceptions).
The script never strips or re-signs the installed app in /Applications (any signature change acts on a copy).
No Bash command executed the script or lldb.

assertions: The reply explains that lldb cannot attach to the signed release (hardened runtime without get-task-allow), which is why the script works on a copy or a source build.
